query: A work-item detail page must render the not-found page when the record is missing, and the create Server Action must redirect to the new item on success. Both paths go through our application boundary.
baseline_failure: RED hypothesis: the agent calls notFound() or redirect() inside the boundary body. Those are implemented by throwing, so the declaration's universal catch converts the framework signal into a typed application failure — the page renders an error state and the redirect never happens, often with a failure kind invented to describe it.
expected_behavior: Keeps the navigation call outside the catch, or re-throws the framework signal before normalising
Has the boundary return not_found as a value and lets the entry point turn it into navigation
Names the guarantee explicitly: 'no thrown value escapes' excludes framework control flow
Adds a test asserting the redirect and the not-found render still occur through the boundary
anti_expectation: Does NOT disable failure normalisation to make navigation work
Does NOT move the business rule into the route to avoid the boundary
Does NOT catch the framework signal and re-issue navigation from a different layer
